l: p
A. When available, on-duty Crisis Intervention Team members shall take primary when responding to calls involving Mental Health Individuals (MHIs) suffering from a mental health condition or crisis.
p

B. Due to the potential for violence present when dealing with persons suffering a mental health crisis, a minimum of two (2) officers shall be dispatched to all calls of this type (including Signal 13 – Mental Health Individual).
p

C. Officers shall, when possible, gather as much information about the subject as is available prior to approaching the person. Officers are encouraged to contact the MHMR (My Health My Resources) Hotline for police only, or have communications do so, for information regarding mental health individual (MHIs) for assistance if it is safe and prudent.
p
D. Officers should use extreme caution in dealing with these potentially dangerous individuals and avoid using any words such as demented or crazy.
p

E. If no criminal offense has occurred and a substantial risk of serious harm does not exist, set an MHMR follow up disposition and add relevant information to the call sheet. CIT will conduct a follow up based on this information.
p

F. A substantial risk of serious harm or death to the person or others may be demonstrated by the person’s statements and/or behavior, actions or evidence of severe emotional distress and deterioration in the person’s mental condition to the extent that the person cannot remain at liberty. The officer may form the belief from the representation of a credible person, on the basis of the statements of harm to self or others, or based on the totality of the conduct of the person and the circumstances under which the person is found. The officer shall take that person into custody for an apprehension by peace officer for emergency detention when these circumstances exist.
p
G. Apprehension by peace officer for emergency detention
p
1. The action taken by a Texas peace officer to detain a person and transport them for a mental health evaluation by a medical professional in the following 48 hours.
p
2. The Health and Safety Code, Chapter 573 sec. 573.001, states that a peace officer, without a warrant, may take a person into custody if the officer has reason to believe and does believe that:
p
a. The person is mentally ill; and
p
b. Because of that mental illness, there is a substantial risk of serious harm to the person, bodily injury or death to others unless the person is immediately restrained; and
p
c. The officer believes that there is not sufficient time to obtain a warrant before taking the person into custody.
p
d. The totality of the circumstances determines the applicability if the notification of emergency detention.

items.t: POLICE ACTIONS WHERE NO CRIMINAL OFFENSE IS INVOLVED
l: p
A. When police officers come into contact with an individual under circumstances meeting the requirements of TX HSC Section 573.001, the following actions shall be taken:
p
1. The subject shall be taken into custody, restrained, and transported in their police vehicle to John Peter Smith Hospital’s Psychiatric Emergency Center.
p

a. If circumstances dictate an alternate means of transporting the subject to the facility, the officer may find it necessary to utilize ambulance services. Transport by ambulance is only provided if medically required to do so or if the MHI requests. Although the individual is transported by ambulance officers will complete the Peace Officer’s Notification of Detention (previously known as a MAP form) upon arrival at the hospital.
p

b. If an officer is dispatched to a call of an individual under thirteen (13) years of age for a notification of emergency detention, CIT should be contacted. The subject shall be transported to Cook Children’s Medical Center. Adolescents age 13 and older shall be transported to John Peter Smith Psychiatric Emergency Center. All children 12 and under shall be taken to Cook Children’s Medical Center.
p

c. For juveniles placed in handcuffs, officers shall contact Cook Children’s Medical Center to allow at least five (5) minutes room preparation time for the emergency care personnel. Officers should bring the handcuffed juvenile to the treatment area using the ambulance entrance. If appropriate advance notice cannot be given, the officer shall park the police unit at the ambulance entrance, personally notify the emergency care personnel, and hold the juvenile in the vehicle until a room is prepared. TBP 10.02
p
2. Upon arrival at the facility, the officers shall assist medical personnel in restraining the subject, if necessary.
p
3. The officer shall complete a Peace Officer’s Notification of Detention and submit it to the facility.
p
4. The officer shall immediately inform the person orally in simple, nontechnical terms:
p
a. of the reason for the detention and
p
b. that a staff member of the facility will inform the person of the person's rights within 24 hours after the time the person is admitted to a facility
p

5. The officer shall complete an incident report regarding the details of the call. The report shall contain pertinent facts regarding the subject’s actions, those individuals who witnessed the actions, and sufficient detail to explain why the officers determined the subject posed a danger to themselves, the officer, or someone else. The officer shall complete the report by end of shift if on duty, or within 24 hours if off duty, to facilitate notifications to MHMR liaisons who partner with the Crisis Intervention Team (CIT). If the Mental Health Individual (MHI) was/is exhibiting any signs of homicidal violence or a mass casualty incident, the report shall be completed immediately, no matter the circumstance and CIT should be notified.
p

a. The Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA, 42 U.S.C. 1395dd § 1867) requires hospitals having an emergency department to provide stabilizing care for all patients, including those presenting with psychiatric crisis, regardless of their ability to pay.
p
b. If the officer becomes aware of any allegations of an EMTALA violation (i.e. patient was refused treatment at a hospital) the officer shall document this in their report.
p
6. The officers shall leave the facility only after the subject has been transferred to JPS personnel.
p
7. Officers shall tag all body worn and in car camera footage with the “CIT” tag.
p

B. If a person suffering a mental illness is already at a hospital that has an Emergency Department and is considered a patient, officers should assess whether the person poses a substantial risk of serious harm to self or others irrespective of the hospital setting. If the person does pose that risk, the officer shall complete the Peace Officer’s Notification of Emergency Detention and present it to the hospital staff who will then detain the subject and Officers may leave the hospital to complete the required incident report.
p

1. If the officer does not witness behavior or hear statements leading them to believe that the subject is an imminent threat to self or others, then a medical professional, including those who are consulted through Telemedicine or Tele-psychiatrist, must provide a signed, written statement which includes specific observations. The officer shall ensure that the statement provides the necessary information required under HSC Sec. 573.002.
p
2. The subject shall remain in the custody of the hospital and shall NOT be transported by police vehicle to another facility, including John Peter Smith.
p
3. Subjects not yet registered, admitted or currently under treatment by ER staff shall NOT be considered under the care of the hospital ER and shall be treated under GO 330.02(A).

items.t: POLICE ACTIONS WHERE AN OFFENSE IS INVOLVED
l: p

A. When officers arrive on the scene of a call involving a person suffering mental illness, and a criminal offense has been committed by the person suffering a mental illness, the officers shall place the person under arrest for the appropriate offense.
p

B. If the subject poses a substantial risk of serious harm or death to themselves or others, the individual shall be transported immediately to John Peter Smith Hospital Psychiatric Emergency Center through an apprehension by peace officer for emergency detention.
p
C. If the subject is under thirteen (13) years of age, the same requirements apply as under GO 331.02 (A)(1)(b).
p

D. Persons suffering a mental illness, who have committed an offense and have been transported to John Peter Smith Hospital, shall be returned to jail upon determination that the person involved no longer requires hospitalization. If the person is a juvenile and was transported to either Cook Children’s Medical Center or John Peter Smith Hospital, detention will follow out-of-custody arrest procedures under General Orders 341.00.

items.t: REPEATED DEALINGS WITH MENTALLY DISTURBED PERSONS
l: p

When officers deal frequently with a mentally disturbed person and believe that the person is not a danger at this time, but has the potential of becoming a threat to themselves or another if not treated, the officer may request assistance from the on call Crisis Intervention Team (CIT) officer, complete a Mental Health Information Report, or add relevant information to the call sheet and enter Request Mental Health Follow Up (MHMR) on their call disposition.
